newsitem.title: POLAND: OSCE grants prize to Reporters sans Frontieres.
newsitem.headline: OSCE grants prize to Reporters sans Frontieres.

text.p: The parliamentary assembly of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) on Saturday awarded its annual Journalism and Democracy prize to Paris-based media freedom group Reporters sans Frontieres.

The OSCE assembly of around 300 parliamentarians, meeting in Warsaw, said in a statement that the $20,000 prize was meant for journalists who had promoted the 54-nation organisation's principles on human rights and democracy.
It said Reporters sans Frontieres (Reporters without Frontiers), founded in 1985, worked in mostly dangerous areas.

"In covering these precarious areas, several journalists of the association have been imprisoned due to their work," the statement said, adding that the group had also denounced appeals to national, racial or religious hatred.

In a separate statement, Reporters sans Frontieres said the award was largely a recognition of its role in Bosnia where it had worked during the years of heaviest conflict to promote journalism that was independent and open to dialogue.

The group's president, Spanish journalist Fernando Castello, said at the award ceremony that freedom of the press was limited in more than half of all countries in the United Nations, including some OSCE members whose parliaments were represented at the July 5-8 Warsaw meeting.
The prize was first awarded last year when it went to Adam Michnik, editor of Poland's Gazeta Wyborcza daily, who was a prominent dissident before communist rule was toppled in 1989.
The OSCE, originating in the 1970s as a forum for East-West dialogue, groups countries of Europe and the former Soviet Union as well as Canada and the United States.
It is devoted to human rights, democracy and the rule of law. Its tasks now include monitoring elections, preventing conflicts and helping to identify and manage crises.
